title: Prepositional 4: 'о' (About)
description: After 'о' (about), the noun shifts into the prepositional case. Same form rules as for в and на.
descriptionRussian: После 'о' (о чём / о ком) существительное стоит в предложном падеже. Те же формы, что и после в и на.
intro: Three lessons in, this case has meant location. It also means topic, and the forms do not change at all to signal the difference. That is worth absorbing early, because it holds across the whole case system: a Russian case is a shape, not a meaning, and the same shape does several unrelated jobs depending on the word that triggered it. Practically, this lesson lets you say what you are thinking and talking about.
rules: О means 'about' and triggers the prepositional case. The case forms are identical to those after в and на.
Question words: О чём? (About what?) for topics; О ком? (About whom?) for people.
О becomes 'об' before vowel-initial nouns (об Антоне). Today's nouns all start with consonants, so 'о' is the right preposition. Lesson 5 drills the о/об rule.
examples: Я думаю о маме. (I think about mom.) мама → о маме.
Антон говорит о работе. (Anton talks about work.) работа → о работе.
Лена пишет о школе. (Lena writes about school.) школа → о школе.
Мы говорим о Москве. (We talk about Moscow.) Москва → о Москве.
Я читаю о городе. (I'm reading about the city.) город → о городе.

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 2: feminine -а becomes which letter after a preposition?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 2: feminine -а changes to -е in the prepositional case. Работа → на работе. Today's lesson uses 'о' (about) with the same case rules.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is thinking about his brother.
items.hint: О is the third prepositional preposition. What ending does masculine consonant take?
items.explanation: О means 'about' and triggers prepositional, just like в and на. Брат → о брате. The case form is identical: masculine consonant + -е.

items.hint: After о (about), apply the same case rule. Мама ends in -а; what does it become?
items.explanation: О triggers prepositional. Мама → о маме. The 'about' meaning is different from 'in/at,' but the case form is the same. Russians say о маме (about mom), о школе (about school), о работе (about work).

items.promptEnglish: Lena is writing about the city.
items.hint: Same masculine pattern. Город ends in...?
items.explanation: Город → о городе. Masculine consonant + -е. The pattern is consistent across all prepositional triggers (в, на, о).

items.hint: Names follow the same gender rules. Маша is fem -а.
items.explanation: Маша → о Маше. Names take the same forms as common nouns. The -а ending becomes -е regardless of whether the noun is a person, a place, or a thing.

items.hint: Apply the same -а → -е pattern as in Lessons 1 and 2.
items.explanation: Школа → о школе. The same -а → -е pattern you've seen with 'в школе' and 'на работе' works after 'о.' Three prepositions, one case rule.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Фильм is masculine consonant. After 'о' (about), prepositional adds -е → фильме.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The teacher is talking about the film.
errorCorrection.explanation: О means 'about' and triggers the prepositional case; masculine consonant nouns add -е: о фильме. Фильм here is the bare nominative (subject form); after о only the prepositional is correct.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton likes to talk about music.
errorCorrection.explanation: After о, feminine -а nouns swap -а for -е: о музыке. Музыка is the nominative subject form; Russian о always governs the prepositional.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena is writing about her family.
errorCorrection.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in -я take -е in the prepositional, like feminine -а: семья → о семье. Семья is the nominative subject form. After о the noun is always prepositional, so о семье.

minimalPairs.explanation: After 'о' (about), the noun shifts to the prepositional case: маме. The nominative мама would be a subject: 'Мама дома' (Mom is home).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anton is thinking about his brother.
minimalPairs.explanation: After 'о' (about), the noun shifts to the prepositional case: брате. The nominative брат would be a subject: 'Брат работает' (My brother works).

reviewVocab.definition: about (preposition + prepositional, used to express the topic of speaking/thinking/writing)
about what? (the prepositional question word for topics)
reviewVocab.example: О чём ты думаешь? — О работе.

reviewVocab.definition: about whom? (the prepositional question word for people)
reviewVocab.example: О ком вы говорите? — О Маше.
